case_title: B. Virupakshaiah v. State of Karnataka and Ors.
trial_court_outcome: Convicted of conspiracy and murder, sentenced to life imprisonment
neutral_facts: The prosecution case revolves around the testimonies of six eye-witnesses who claimed to have seen four unknown persons assault the occupants of an Indica car, resulting in the death of two individuals. The witnesses initially stated that four persons were involved but later added that there were eight assailants. The prosecution also relied on the recovery of weapons and other articles, but the witnesses involved in the recovery turned hostile. The trial court convicted all twelve accused based on the eye-witness testimonies and the alleged conspiracy to kill the deceased, citing a motive of revenge. The High Court, however, acquitted the accused due to inconsistencies in the eye-witness accounts, lack of identification of the accused, and the absence of cogent evidence to prove the conspiracy and the recovery of weapons.
